records.title: Ridge Regression: Structure, Cross-Validation, and Sketching
records.abstract: The study analyzes ridge estimation, regularization selection through cross-validation, and sketching approximations.
records.text: Frozen source synopsis, not a full-text copy. Ridge Regression: Structure, Cross-Validation, and Sketching, sections 2 and 3, studies squared-error fitting with a quadratic coefficient penalty and selection of regularization through held-out/cross-validation error. The closed-form ridge solution depends on the feature covariance and regularization strength. The paper discusses validation bias in a high-dimensional asymptotic regime. It does not identify an optimal polynomial degree or alpha for this task; those must be measured from the supplied public training and validation data. Mathematical facts are literature context, not local experimental evidence.

records.title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems
records.abstract: The original study motivates regularization for ill-conditioned regression designs and analyzes the bias and variance of ridge estimates.
records.text: Frozen authored source synopsis, not a full-text copy. The original paper considers linear regression when the feature covariance is poorly conditioned. Adding a nonnegative diagonal term yields biased ridge coefficient estimates. Sections on ridge regression and mean-square error analyze how regularization can reduce estimator variance while introducing bias, and present a ridge trace for sensitivity analysis. These parameter-estimation results motivate comparing regularized and unregularized polynomial features. They do not establish that any chosen degree or penalty improves validation prediction on the supplied task. That claim requires actual trusted-host measurements under the fixed train/validation split.

records.applicability: Ill-conditioned linear coefficient estimation; motivation for a measured polynomial-ridge comparison, not a task optimum or a local result.

records.title: Smoothing noisy data with spline functions: Estimating the correct degree of smoothing by the method of generalized cross-validation
records.abstract: The publisher original Summary describes choosing smoothing strength for noisy observations by generalized cross-validation.
records.text: Frozen authored source synopsis based only on the publisher original Summary, not a full-paper reproduction. The paper considers smoothing splines with a squared fitting error and a roughness penalty. Generalized cross-validation selects the smoothing parameter using residual error adjusted by the smoothing matrix trace, aiming to approximate prediction-risk selection without requiring a known noise variance. The stated analysis uses regular-mesh and asymptotic assumptions. This supports treating regularization selection as an evidence-dependent task, but it neither evaluates the supplied polynomial ridge implementation nor supplies local validation measurements. Spline smoothness, polynomial degree and ridge coefficient penalty are different controls; no equivalence or guaranteed improvement is assumed.
